content: 1. If Guillain-Barré syndrome has occurred within six weeks of receiving a previous vaccine containing tetanus toxoid, the decision to administer any tetanus toxoid-containing vaccine, including HIBERIX, should be made after a thorough evaluation of the potential benefits and risks. 2. The tip caps of the prefilled syringes may contain natural rubber latex, which could trigger allergic reactions in individuals who are sensitive to latex. 3. Syncope (fainting) can occur following the administration of injectable vaccines, including HIBERIX. This fainting episode may be accompanied by temporary neurological symptoms such as visual disturbances, paresthesia (tingling or numbness), and tonic-clonic limb movements. Measures should be in place to prevent injuries from falls and to restore adequate blood flow to the brain in the event of syncope. 4. Before administering the vaccine, healthcare providers should review the patient’s immunization history to identify any potential hypersensitivity to vaccines. Epinephrine and other appropriate agents for managing immediate allergic reactions must be readily available in case an acute anaphylactic reaction occurs. 5. The safety and effectiveness of HIBERIX in immunosuppressed children have not been established. If HIBERIX is administered to immunosuppressed children, including those undergoing immunosuppressive therapy, the expected immune response may not be achieved. 6. Urine antigen detection may not provide reliable diagnostic information for suspected Haemophilus influenzae type b disease within one to two weeks after receiving a vaccine containing Haemophilus influenzae type b, including HIBERIX. 7. Immunization with HIBERIX does not replace routine tetanus immunization.
